summary: Frontend-only verification of Clients CRUD UI and login brute-force lockout message. All specified flows PASS.
verified_flows: Admin login (admin/admin123) succeeds; sidebar shows Manage > Clients.
GET /clients renders 'API Clients' card + New Client button (clients-add) with empty state (clients-empty-add). No crash.

Create client 'Mobile App' with scopes read+users -> key-reveal dialog shows key starting with 'ak_' in client-key-value (ak_286c511d...). Copy icon click works (no error). Done closes dialog; row appears with masked key, read/users badges, Active status.
Regenerate: confirm dialog appears; new key dialog shows a DIFFERENT ak_ key (ak_857226487...); client remains Active.
Revoke: confirm dialog; status badge switches to 'Revoked'; revoke button disappears for inactive client.
Delete: confirm dialog; row removed from table.

Brute-force lockout on throwaway 'lockme2@example.com': attempts 1-2 show 'Invalid credentials.', attempts 3-4 show '2/1 attempt(s) left before lockout.', attempt 5 returns HTTP 429 with 'Too many failed attempts. Login locked for 15 minutes.' rendered in login-error-alert.
After brute-force, admin/admin123 login still works (per IP+identifier lockout scope confirmed).
seed_data_creation: One temporary client 'Mobile App' created and deleted during test. lockme2@example.com is now IP+identifier locked for ~15 min.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login submit testid is 'login-submit-button' (not 'login-submit'). Backend surfaces graduated lockout warnings ('N attempt(s) left before lockout.') then final 429 'Too many failed attempts. Login locked for 15 minutes.' — both surfaced via login-error-alert.
